looked_at.what: The lecturer says to evaluate each derivative of the general function at x=0.
The lecturer says the coefficient of each x^n term is the nth derivative evaluated at zero, divided by n factorial.
For a new center a, the lecturer says to use powers of x-a and evaluate all derivatives of f at a.
The lecturer says every coefficient is divided by the appropriate factorial to cancel repeated power-rule factors.

steps.question: What is the old center used in the displayed general polynomial?
steps.answer_text: The old center is 0: the coefficients use f and its derivatives evaluated at 0, and the terms use powers x^n.
steps.why: At 725.9-743.6 s the transcript says to evaluate derivatives at x=0 and describes the coefficient of x^n as the nth derivative at zero divided by n factorial.

steps.question: What changes when the center is renamed a?
steps.answer_text: The value becomes f(a), every derivative evaluation moves from 0 to a, and every power x^n becomes (x-a)^n.
steps.why: At 784.7-799.1 s the transcript says the new input is called a, the polynomial is written in powers of x-a, and all derivatives of f are evaluated at a; f(a) is the zeroth-derivative case.

steps.question: Do the factorial denominators change with the center?
steps.answer_text: No. The nth-order term remains divided by n!, including the same 0!, 1!, 2!, and so on.
steps.why: At 732.5-743.6 s the nth coefficient is divided by n!, and at 697.0-704.6 s factorials are explained as correcting repeated power-rule factors, which is independent of the center.

answer: The three simultaneous substitutions are: f(0) -> f(a); f'(0), f''(0), ..., f^(n)(0) -> f'(a), f''(a), ..., f^(n)(a); and x, x^2, ..., x^n -> (x-a), (x-a)^2, ..., (x-a)^n. The factorial denominators do not change: each nth-order term is still divided by n! (so the same 0!, 1!, 2!, ... remain).
basis: Transcript: 725.9-743.6 s says derivatives are evaluated at zero and the x^n coefficient is the nth derivative divided by n!; 784.7-799.1 s says that for center a the powers are x-a and all derivatives are evaluated at a. The f(0)->f(a) substitution is the n=0 (function-value) case. At 697.0-704.6 s the factorial is tied to cancelling repeated power-rule factors, so it is unchanged by shifting the center.
